title: Establish intake & prioritization flow for customer optimization/advisory requests (batching, caching, quantization, routing)
creator: Maya Nguyen
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable intake and prioritization workflow for enterprise customer requests that ask for optimization/advisory work: tuning batching/caching knobs, recommending quantization profiles, and setting routing policies. Today requests flow ad-hoc via support and AE threads which leads to slow response times and inconsistent outcomes.

Background & problem statement:
- Large enterprise customers frequently ask for performance/cost optimization help. These requests range from quick config changes (batch size, cache TTL) to deeper work (quantization evaluation, custom routing policies).
- Engineering triage is overloaded; we lack consistent data about workload shape, current config, and expected business outcomes.
- Without a formal intake we risk overcommitting engineering time and delivering inconsistent recommendations that cause regressions or higher latency.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Define intake form + required data points for advisory/optimization requests.
- Create prioritization rubric mapping request type, expected ROI, customer tier, SLA, and security constraints to priority.
- Build a lightweight process to hand off to Solutions/Platform Eng: routing, quick-reject criteria, and expected response times.
- Produce an internal template for advisory runbooks (tunable knobs, measurement checklist, rollback steps).

Out of scope:
- Implementing automated tuning engine (future work).
- Deep engineering changes to runtime (separate ENG epics).

Acceptance criteria:
- A completed intake form template (Confluence) that includes mandatory observability snapshots, token & throughput profiles, peak windows, and example prompts.
- Prioritization rubric documented and validated with Sales and SE (signed off).
- Decision matrix that routes requests to either: Solutions Engineering (quick config), Platform Eng (investigation), or product backlog (feature request).
- One pilot run with a named enterprise customer (Customer: Heliotrope Health) and documented outcome.

Proposed intake form required fields (short):
- Customer name, contact, and tier
- Endpoint(s) or model versions in use
- Current config: batch sizes, cache TTLs, KV cache enabled, quantization variant, region/routing preferences
- Typical qps, p95 latency, and token distribution (short/long sequences)
- A small reproducible prompt set and expected quality thresholds
- Cost & SLA goals (e.g., reduce per-token cost by 20% or p95 < 200ms)
- Access scope: can we access logs/metrics/trace IDs? (yes/no)
- Security classification (public/PII/regulated)

Prioritization rubric (summary):
- Priority factors: customer_tier(enterprise>startup), ROI_estimate (>20% cost savings), risk_of_regression (high if quantization requested), compliance constraints, time_sensitivity.
- Example mapping: enterprise + high ROI + low risk => P0/P1; experimental quantization for regulated data => backlog + security_review_required.

Operational SLA proposals:
- Initial triage: 3 business days
- Quick advisory (configuration-only): 7 business days to delivery + documentation
- Deeper engineering investigation: estimated within 10 business days with a proposed plan

Runbook template (to be added to Confluence):
- Snapshot collection checklist (metrics, traces, sample prompts)
- Safe tuning steps for batching and cache (order of changes, expected metric impacts)
- Quantization advisory: test profile steps, quality regression checkpoints, rollback steps
- Routing policy advisory: simulation approach, fallback rules, canary rollout plan

KPIs to measure success:
- Mean time to first response for advisory requests
- % of requests resolved without engineering code changes
- Customer satisfaction scores post-advisory

Notes on trade-offs:
- Faster SLAs require Solutions Eng bandwidth; we propose gating by customer tier and expected ROI.
- Quantization guidance carries higher regression risk; require a tested evaluation harness before advising for production.
- Automated tuning is desirable but not part of this phase; keep intake data structured for future automation.
